sampling_method: A = every merged.json row with a key rename (OGra11, RagaWill18, HaonEtal16, YingEtal92; no duplicates or collisions in postcheck.json), an ENTRYTYPE change (13), identity_quote_failed (LohnEtal09), verdict ambiguous/no_source (18), or a researcher-named different version/replacement candidate (deBr24, vond81, VaswEtal17, Laks01, Schl07, Stra06); no DOI was dropped or changed (WangEtal10b only lowercased) = 37. Suffixed keys whose target_base drops the letter (action keep) are not renames. Pool = sorted remaining keys (73); B = random.Random(20261003).sample(pool, round(len(pool)/2)) = 36. Re-fetched per entry: api.crossref.org (1 req/s) for every DOI, SfN OASIS ViewAbstract pages (browser UA) and the SfN 2005 archive page, PMLR, papers.nips.cc BibTeX, BnF SRU, the Moth, SciPy proceedings, Google Patents, archive.org/Wayback PDFs, CORE, Dartmouth Primo, PubMed efetch (DankEtal08). DBLP was behind a bot wall. FINAL merged.json values judged field by field.
systematic_findings: POST-CHECK/FORMATTER changes names the researcher left alone: an unbraced two-word surname or given name is abbreviated to initials, and merged.json still labels the change source "researcher". Wrong for CarvEtal22b and TianEtal20b (A Quattrini Li -> A Q Li; his surname is Quattrini Li, as in all three HEAD entries). Plausible but unrequested for SingEtal24 (K Vasuden Alwala -> K V Alwala, K Hou U -> K H U, V Satish Kumar -> V S Kumar). This goes against POSTCHECK.md ("never adds or removes an initial"; "Author values change only as the researcher proposed them"). Suggest bracing compound surnames when cdl.bib already writes them spaced (A {Quattrini Li}), and a check that a final value differs from the researcher value only in labelled rule changes.

POST-CHECK print_year_conflict false alarms: ReccOKee89 (read "pre-2000" in the notes as a print date, suggests year 2000) and VaswEtal17 (Curran reprint "printed 2018" for NeurIPS 2017). LiuEtal18/LiuWang16 (outside the sample) are the same NeurIPS/Curran pattern. Flags only, nothing applied, but they add noise to the user queue.

POST-CHECK ENTRYTYPE: @conference -> @inproceedings is applied even when the researcher says there is no proceedings (Laks01, a speech; the researcher suggested @misc). A @conference/@inproceedings with no proceedings should be left for the user.

RESEARCHER: vanVEtal05 did not add the printed initial K ("van Vugt, M. K.") under an invented "no initial on a braced particle surname" rule. Wech97 moved "Third Edition" into an Edition field on a @misc, where standard styles do not print it, and misstated that Wech08 has an edition field. Hwang consistency: vanVEtal05 G Hwang-Grodzins (SfN 2005 byline "Hwang-Grodzins, G.") and DankEtal08 G M Hwang (PubMed "Hwang Grace M", PDF "Grace M. Hwang") are each right for their own byline. The same person is printed under two names, so the user should decide whether to unify (HEAD has 1 Hwang-Grodzins and 3 G Hwang entries).
